title: Reconcile current project status and remove contradictory live claims
work: Reconcile current-entry docs against the release and live receipts; retain historical reports with dated labels; distinguish scripts from browser signing.
acceptance: Current guides consistently describe deployed Core, partial receipt coverage, disabled native faucet, unsupported services and test-only results.

title: Confirm registration and complete the check-in requirements
work: Confirm team registration and actual submission state; assemble progress, remaining work, repo, architecture, deployment receipt and demo link; ask the organiser about recovery if the deadline was missed.
acceptance: Founder retains actual submission confirmation or organiser response. No registration or submission is claimed without evidence.
founderConfirmedStatus: Founder reports Submit Build/check-in action completed; no entry URL independently verified.
remaining: Retain acknowledgement in founder account; report any organiser correction.

title: Select awards based on demonstrated scope
work: Prioritise Ecosystem DApps; map working SDK capabilities to Middleware; confirm multiple-track eligibility and prize stacking with organiser if ambiguous; keep undeployed bridge claims out.
acceptance: A dated track decision links each claim to working evidence and records any unanswered organiser question.

title: Publish a reproducible architecture and setup guide
work: Diagram browser wallet, native modules, Core, RPC, serverless API, Blob and separate issuer; distinguish trust boundaries; run fresh-install setup and disclose third-party dependencies.
acceptance: A new contributor follows the guide; clean install/build succeeds; diagram matches deployed components and includes no secrets.

title: Produce the final three-minute demonstration
work: Show customer problem, wallet steps, actual records, native integration, results and limitations; use historical finalized receipts when replaying evidence rather than pretending new transactions occurred. Prefer separate-user browser evidence when available; if it is not available, use the completed script receipts and explicitly disclose that limit rather than delaying eligibility or implying live signing.
acceptance: Public video is at most three minutes, accessible without login, and shows an understandable product flow with verified evidence.

title: Prepare a fact-checked pitch deck
work: Cover customer pain, product, why Portaldot, actual delivery, revenue hypothesis, costs, pilot status, risks and next milestones; founder supplies team and customer facts in their own words.
acceptance: Accessible deck separates completed work, assumptions and planned capabilities; no invented partners, traction or returns.

title: Create a final release and code-freeze checklist
work: Maintain meaningful incremental commits; record release commit/deployment/test evidence; verify demo and links before freeze; follow organiser process for serious post-freeze fixes.
acceptance: A tagged/referenced release, test manifest and final submission checklist exist before the official freeze; no late core dump or fabricated history.

title: Verify the real Portaldot extension flow
work: Check provider identity and official install destination; share accounts, select one, reject a request, reconnect and sign a low-cost native action; keep Portaldot first.
acceptance: Real extension observations and one approved finalized action are recorded. Mocked tests are not presented as real-wallet verification.

title: Verify account mapping and account-switch safety
work: Test mapped/unmapped accounts, mapping collisions, network changes and switching accounts while review is open; keep native batches flat and bind plans to the actual signer.
acceptance: Wrong account/network invalidates review; no local key fallback; mapping succeeds with the correct native account or fails explicitly.

title: Publish an honest wallet compatibility matrix
work: Verify each supported injected wallet separately; explain why ordinary MetaMask EVM signing cannot sign the native flow; keep EVM-only tooling separate.
acceptance: UI and guide list only tested support, clear prerequisites and verified install links; no recovery-phrase import is introduced.

title: Add an intent-based first-use journey
work: Let visitors choose operating an asset, reviewing/funding, or inspecting the project; allow public browsing; route each role to one clear next step without creating an account.
acceptance: A first-time visitor identifies the product purpose, intended role and next action without help; no wallet or fabricated balance is generated.

title: Show wallet and service readiness before actions
work: Display actual native/payment balances, selected account, chain, contract and API readiness; distinguish zero, loading, unavailable, wrong network and missing extension.
acceptance: A disconnected or unfunded visitor receives the correct next action. Connection alone never implies all funding services are ready.

title: Show action costs including storage deposits
work: Separate purchase/bond amount, protocol fees, native execution fee, storage deposit and possible refund; estimate against current state and expire quotes when identity/state changes.
acceptance: Quotes show source/time and limits; unknown costs remain unknown; reviewed fees plus deposits are not described as gas alone; cap rejection never triggers an automatic higher-cap retry.

title: Make faucet prerequisites and limits understandable
work: Explain native tPOT versus test pUSD, official allocation path, daily reset, service reserve and failed requests; link to verified organiser instructions.
acceptance: User can tell which token is missing and how to obtain it; hosted native faucet stays disabled and deployer funds are never automatically distributed.

title: Save an unsigned listing draft without secrets
work: Preserve form progress, validate photo and input limits, show a summary before signing and warn if uploaded public data should not be shared; exclude wallet secrets.
acceptance: Refresh restores a draft with an explicit save/clear policy; changing a wallet does not silently change operator identity; nothing is published without approval.

title: Make transaction states and finality unambiguous
work: Expose preparing, awaiting wallet, submitted, included, finalized, rejected, failed and unconfirmed states; prevent duplicate clicks and keep completed receipts visible.
acceptance: Rejection, dropped/usurped transaction and delayed finality are distinguishable; only a successful finalized receipt is called successful.

title: Resume partial document uploads safely
work: Persist accepted content hashes and finalized anchors; retry only missing document publication; revalidate allocated identifiers before later creation; retain completed upload receipts.
acceptance: Terms success/photo failure and pin failure recover without duplicate stores or listing creation; changed IDs require rebuilding and reviewing immutable terms.

title: Reconcile unknown outcomes before retrying
work: Retain public action identifiers, signer/network identity and known hashes; inspect finalized history/catalog/nonce as appropriate; expose publication-only retry when chain execution succeeded.
acceptance: A timeout or refresh cannot blindly resubmit an already successful money-moving action. Recovery is demonstrated without additional duplicate spending.

title: Build a receipt and history centre
work: Show action, actor, finalized block/hash, status, actual amounts and known fee data; support copy, verified explorer links where available, and export.
acceptance: History reconciles with contract totals, labels incomplete coverage, and offers useful recovery paths without exposing signing material.

title: Exercise rejection and interruption scenarios
work: Test rejection at every signing step, account/network change, API failure after finalization, tab refresh and double-click; preserve the current wallet rather than substituting identities.
acceptance: A recorded scenario matrix proves no false success, key fallback or unintended repeat transaction; regressions protect material failure paths.

title: Fix sold-out, connecting and unavailable action states
work: Replace stale undeployed messages during loading/outages; clearly explain sold-out offers and unavailable pools; separate user-owned shares from stake and sale inventory.
acceptance: The existing test offer is honestly shown as sold out, not broken; loading does not assert the deployed contract is absent; unsupported actions are not advertised as ready.

title: Prove the browser flow with separate operator and participant accounts
work: Prepare a bounded plan, funded native accounts and approved test-token source; perform website approvals and reconcile balances; reuse existing assets for share/stake checks where possible and label historical creation separately.
acceptance: Actual separate-account browser results are recorded. No extra listing or live write occurs without a costed budget; script evidence and browser evidence remain distinct.

title: Add an operator and asset evidence checklist
work: Record operator identity/source, equipment documents, business revenue source, schedule, verifier, date and review state; distinguish self-reported, hash-checked and independently checked evidence.
acceptance: Every badge states who checked what and when; blockchain presence is never represented as independent physical or legal verification.

title: Improve image quality and verify photo integrity
work: Validate size/type, preserve useful resolution when compressing, preview the exact bytes, verify content hash/availability independently of terms, and provide accessible fallbacks.
acceptance: New uploads are legible on desktop/mobile within limits; a failed photo has its own state. Existing immutable low-resolution test media is not silently replaced with different bytes.

title: Make the operator workspace actionable
work: Show each asset, funding status, available sale inventory, bond, payment deadline, deposits and next action using chain-backed data; surface overdue/defaulted items.
acceptance: An operator can determine what needs attention and reach deposit/top-up/closure actions without navigating developer tools; missing counters stay unavailable.

title: Explain actual deposits and payment-clock behaviour
work: Show gross deposit, actual fee, net allocation and qualifying status; distinguish the initial payment window from an actual payment and projected income from paid income.
acceptance: The 1 test-pUSD deposit reconciles to 0.005 fee and 0.995 allocation; timestamps never imply payment when only listing initialization occurred.

title: Export useful funding and payment reports
work: Export verified receipts, amounts, currency/decimals, period and account identifiers; include coverage and testnet labels; retain exact source units and usable timestamps.
acceptance: CSV/report totals match included receipts, disclose exclusions and do not invent complete accounting or customer revenue.

title: Explain default, bond recovery and exit
work: Explain cadence, overdue/default states, slashing, top-up, wind-down, unstaking, selling and bond limits; distinguish return of shares from repayment of purchase money.
acceptance: A user can explain how they might exit, what happens if there is no buyer, and why a bond does not insure their full capital; controls match deployed rules.

title: Make discovery honest and useful
work: Filter/search actual catalog entries; visibly label the authorized test listing and completed offer; show unavailable data correctly; avoid mixing illustrative graphics with asset evidence.
acceptance: No generated business listings, invented totals or automatic opening balances appear; test records cannot be mistaken for genuine financed equipment.

title: Clarify portfolio ownership, stake and claims
work: Separate owned shares, earning stake, pending deposited income and previously claimed income; keep claims visible after zero stake; explain stake/unstake effects.
acceptance: Balances match native assets and Core state, including zero-stake pending claims; no projected return is displayed as money already earned.

title: Define receipt coverage and reconcile history
work: Maintain honest partial coverage for app-published receipts; reconcile totals and imports; specify an archive-backed full-index path only if available; paginate Blob listings.
acceptance: Externally submitted transactions cannot silently become zero income or disappear behind a complete-history claim; pagination and reconciliation are tested.

title: Prove document durability and recovery
work: Back up immutable verified bytes and anchors; test recovery after native retention expires and storage/API outages; document any renewal service separately with its own budget.
acceptance: Hash-verified documents remain recoverable after a restart/restore test; renewal is not promised unless running and monitored; missing bytes never receive substitute content.

title: Verify read consistency and stale-quote handling
work: Use clearly identified finalized snapshots where needed; enforce genesis/code/payment-asset identity; refresh sale inventory, allowance and balances before signing.
acceptance: A stale listing/quote or mismatched chain/code fails safely and prompts a new review; no configured payment asset is silently substituted.

title: Harden concurrent faucet requests and issuer spending
work: Review atomic account/day claims, global quota races, issuer nonce serialization, rate limits, ambiguous mint recovery and gas reserve enforcement; load-test with isolated fixtures.
acceptance: Concurrent requests cannot duplicate grants or accidentally exceed the defined service budget; no deployment key is used; unknown mint outcomes are reconciled before retry.

title: Triage and patch dependency advisories
work: Reproduce the reported Zod advisory chain through Blob/OIDC/CLI configuration, inspect runtime reachability, choose a compatible fix, regenerate a clean lockfile and rerun relevant checks.
acceptance: Record affected versions, fix or justified mitigation, clean-install/build results and remaining advisories; do not apply blind force upgrades or assume a passing audit proves safety.

title: Review contract and native-backing boundaries
work: Review direct callers bypassing web checks, supported token identities, existing default guards, bond solvency, malicious callbacks, native fractionalization lock and who can burn/redeem a deed. Explicitly assess direct-to-operator purchase transfers and missing spending controls. Design, without deploying, funding escrow/targets/deadlines, vendor or milestone release, independent approval, refunds/disputes and accountable collections; keep custody/eligibility review in B06/B07.
acceptance: An adversarial review maps each protection to contract, runtime, web or business process; deployed protections remain covered; any new bytecode needs a separately approved migration budget. Current limits and proposed controls are visibly separate; no purchase-money escrow or regulatory protection is claimed for Core v1. A proposed release model identifies approvers, evidence, conflicts, costs and failure cases before any new bytecode or real-money use.

title: Add reproducible continuous checks and release evidence
work: Run relevant contract, SDK, server, web, type and build checks in CI; protect secrets; verify a clean lockfile install and meaningful regressions; record skipped live tests honestly.
acceptance: A contributor can reproduce the checks and identify the release commit; failures block release without spending faucet tokens automatically.

title: Reduce initial load and measure mobile performance
work: Split optional routes and heavy SDK imports, defer advanced tooling and avoid blocking the homepage on RPC; measure before/after on a representative mobile profile.
acceptance: A recorded baseline and improved startup measurement exist; key routes still work and visual polish is preserved; no arbitrary score is claimed without measurement.

title: Define hosting, backup, secret and incident operations
work: Document production configuration and permissions, issuer rotation, separate service budgets, storage/hosting limits, health monitoring, rollback and restoration.
acceptance: A recovery drill restores verified data; no deployer secret is hosted or committed; an operator knows how to disable a failing service and investigate safely.

title: Handle RPC/API latency and outages professionally
work: Bound requests, clean up subscriptions, expose retryable read states and partial service readiness, prevent noisy retry loops and distinguish stale data from current observations.
acceptance: RPC disconnect, missing Blob data, non-JSON response and function timeout show a useful state without fabricated data or automatic transaction resubmission.

title: Interview reachable operators and identify the paid problem
work: Speak with the solar operator and the other reachable group; ask about the last actual funding/payment/reporting problem, current tools, time/cost and evidence-sharing permissions.
acceptance: Dated notes distinguish observed pain, willingness to share data and objections; no contact or partnership is claimed merely because the founder can reach the company.

title: Agree a small testnet pilot with a real operator
work: Define one operator, permitted non-sensitive asset information, roles, success measures, timeline and consent; keep actual money and public claims outside the testnet pilot.
acceptance: A specific pilot agreement or clear refusal is retained; operator-approved information is not uploaded publicly without permission.

title: Validate the actual asset cash-flow story
work: Inspect permitted equipment costs, collections, operating costs, bond affordability, proposed payment schedule and capital/exit expectations; distinguish records from illustrative arithmetic.
acceptance: An operator-approved example shows where funder payments could come from, funding shortfalls and downside cases; no returns or repayment guarantee is inferred.

title: Test pricing and willingness to pay
work: Present funding administration, reporting and payout-management options; distinguish deployed 1% sale/0.5% deposit fees from unimplemented subscription/onboarding hypotheses.
acceptance: At least one specific price/offer receives a documented accept, reject or conditional response; interest is not reported as paying revenue.

title: Calculate viable cost per operator and offering
work: Include support, acquisition, verification, legal/payment providers, storage, hosting, collections and failed transactions; separate refundable locks, user funds and company income.
acceptance: A scenario model with labelled assumptions shows contribution at realistic volumes and identifies a viable fee/minimum deal size or a reason the model fails.

title: Define rights, obligations and eligible real-money users
work: For a first permitted market, obtain qualified review of equipment ownership, offering rights, custody, agreements, identity, transfers, disputes, default and exit; document global expansion constraints.
acceptance: A reviewed operating model states who owes what and who may participate; testnet records are never treated as sufficient legal ownership or universal approval.

title: Design real collections, payouts and custody responsibility
work: Choose who collects customer income, converts currency if needed, holds funds, reconciles records and pays funders; evaluate eligible payment providers only when requirements are known.
acceptance: A feasible supported payment path and responsible parties are documented before implementation; no synthetic bank integration or unsupported global cash-out promise.

title: Make an evidence-based continue-or-adjust decision
work: Evaluate demand, evidence quality, operator economics and willingness to pay; if funding is unsuitable but reporting/payout administration is valuable, evaluate that narrower product.
acceptance: A written decision names supporting evidence, failed assumptions and next experiment; marketplace expansion is not justified by development effort already spent.

title: Polish the existing brand and visual hierarchy
work: Retain a consistent logo, color, type and spacing system; fix low-quality new media handling, dropdown alignment, form layouts and understandable primary actions.
acceptance: Homepage explains who Portion serves and what to do; asset evidence stays distinguishable from decorative illustrations; desktop/mobile screenshots show consistent quality.

title: Make motion, mobile and accessibility support the task
work: Use purposeful transitions for steps, approvals and feedback; honor reduced motion; test keyboard/focus, contrast, errors and narrow layouts on key journeys.
acceptance: Key flows work without animation or a mouse, dialogs preserve focus, controls have useful labels and no essential content overflows the tested mobile widths.

title: Run first-time-user usability sessions
work: Ask new users to explain the product, inspect an asset, understand costs and find operator/funder actions; observe confusion rather than teaching through the test.
acceptance: Dated observations and fixes show users can identify purpose and next actions; number of participants and limits are disclosed rather than claiming broad usability proof.

title: Prepare evidence-based marketing and judge journeys
work: Lead with the paid problem and working testnet flow; provide short role-specific guidance and a verifiable evidence trail; distinguish self-funded test activity from customers.
acceptance: Every capability/traction claim is supported or labelled planned; founder approves external messages and destinations before anything is sent or posted.

title: Measure product friction with a privacy-conscious plan
work: Define completion, abandonment, failure and support metrics; prefer consented observations first and collect no keys, recovery words or unnecessary wallet-linked identity.
acceptance: A measurement plan states purpose, retention and consent; any implemented analytics are tested and actual observations are separated from targets.

title: Maintain an explicit native-token budget and reserve
work: Refresh actual balances before any write; budget fees, storage, refunds and failure costs by action; record service wallets separately; use existing receipts/read-only checks before repeating creation.
acceptance: Every new live test has a reviewed cap and remaining reserve. Last verified 44.82920824 tPOT is labelled a dated balance; no new deployment, faucet request or chain write is implied by this backlog.

title: Document protocol cost limits and funded-account prerequisites
work: Explain why testnet deposits are high; preserve the 32-byte hash saving; measure per-listing/participant costs without stripping protections; plan separate funded tester accounts through official channels.
acceptance: Costs are reproducible and distinguish caps from charges; ordinary users know native funds are required; any extra token request is truthful and explicitly authorized.

title: Gate bridge, node-tool and keeper expansion
work: Keep unproven bridge, pools, automated slashing/renewal/compounding and complete archive indexing out of the primary promise; define a customer or award-evidence gate for each later project.
acceptance: Advanced pages state actual readiness; no new deployment or spend is scheduled merely to claim more tracks; core usability remains the priority.
